prompt.context: Your client is a large, private financial services company. They are the largest 401k provider in the US with over $5T assets under management. However, they are seeing tightening margins on their financial products and have approached your firm for help. The majority of their customers are aged 55+ and are fearing their ability to afford rising retirement costs.
prompt.question: What are some potential avenues for revenue growth?

clarifying_info.q: Where is the client headquartered and what is their geographic footprint?
clarifying_info.a: Headquartered in Boston; serves customers through 10 regional offices and more than 190 Investor Centers in the United States; global presence spans eight other countries across North America, Europe, Asia, and Australia.

clarifying_info.q: What products does the client currently offer?
clarifying_info.a: Financial planning and retirement options such as IRAs, annuities, and managed accounts; brokerage and cash management products; college savings accounts; and other financial services for millions of individual investors. The client works with employers to build benefit programs and offers clearing, custody, investment products, brokerage, and trading services. The client is NOT a bank and does NOT currently offer any loan products.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's business model / how do they earn revenue?
clarifying_info.a: They earn basis-point fees on assets under management. Current margins are down due to the rise of robo-advisors.
The client is the market share leader. Detailed competitor financial information is not available.
The majority of customers are 55+. The general population trend of 10,000 retiring Americans daily has prompted the client to review new products targeting this customer base.

exhibits.title: Home Equity Products for Retirees
exhibits.shows: A matrix or comparison of existing products that allow retirees to extract equity from their homes, categorized along dimensions such as cost to the customer (high vs. low) and potentially market size or growth trend.
exhibits.data: Products shown include: Refinance, Home Equity Loan, Home Equity Line of Credit (HELOC), and Reverse Mortgages. Axes or labels indicate cost to the customer and likely growth/size dimensions.

framework: Existing vs. new customers (Ansoff-style 2x2: existing/new products × existing/new customers)
Existing products: assess current product profitability and pricing power
New products for existing customers: identify unmet needs of 55+ retirees (e.g., liquidity, healthcare cost funding)
New customers: assess feasibility of expanding beyond core 55+ demographic
Competitive landscape: who else serves this space and what would differentiation look like
Entry strategy: build internally, borrow (partner/license), or buy (acquire)
Market size: size the opportunity for the most promising new product
Risks and regulatory considerations: financial services regulation, consumer protection, brand risk

questions.prompt: The client is primarily interested in entering the mortgage lending market. Loans would be targeted to retired customers aged 55+ to help them extract equity from their homes to pay for everyday living expenses. What should the client consider when evaluating entering this market?
questions.guidance: Candidate should cover: (1) Competitive advantage — what existing capabilities (customer relationships, AUM, brand trust) give the client an edge in mortgage lending; (2) Revenue model — origination fees (1-2% of loan value); (3) Scalability — can the solution reach the 55+ customer base at scale through existing channels; (4) Market size — how large is the addressable retiree home-equity market; (5) Customer willingness to pay / borrow; (6) Competition — existing lenders, banks; (7) Regulatory restrictions — lending regulations, consumer-protection rules for seniors; (8) Entry strategy — build, partner, or acquire a lending capability.

questions.prompt: Here is data on existing products that help retirees extract equity from their homes (Exhibit 1). What are your insights?
questions.guidance: Strong candidate observations: (1) Most home loan products are NOT focused on the retiree market because they all require a debt-to-income ratio for approval — retirees without pension income cannot qualify; (2) Reverse mortgages are predatory and the client would never offer them for brand-protection reasons; (3) Home Equity Loans and HELOCs are growing, signaling customer demand; (4) There is a large, underserved opportunity space for a retiree-focused product that sits below reverse mortgages in terms of predatory risk but fills the gap left by DTI-gated products. Market sizes (if candidate asks): Refinance $900B, Home Equity Loan $300B, HELOC $150B, Reverse Mortgages $10B.

math.setup: Market size context — if candidate asks for numbers: Refinance $900B, Home Equity Loan $300B, HELOC $150B, Reverse Mortgages $10B.
steps: Note that most of the large markets (Refinance, Home Equity Loan, HELOC) require debt-to-income approval, excluding income-poor retirees
Reverse Mortgages ($10B) serve retirees but are predatory — client will not pursue
Opportunity: a new retiree-focused home-equity product that does not require DTI approval and is not predatory sits between HELOC and Reverse Mortgages
math.answer: There is an underserved retiree segment that cannot access mainstream home-equity products due to DTI requirements, and will not use predatory reverse mortgages. A new product designed for this segment represents a meaningful white-space opportunity.

questions.prompt: How would you go about sizing the market for this opportunity?
questions.guidance: Candidate should explain the process and data needed rather than diving straight into arithmetic. Key data points to collect: (1) Total US population aged 60+ who own a home; (2) Percentage of those homeowners with meaningful extractable equity; (3) Percentage of those homeowners who need cash (i.e., face a retirement funding gap). Revenue model: lender earns origination fees of approximately 1-2% of total loan value. Candidate should ask for industry-average origination fee if not already provided.

math.setup: Revenue = (# eligible retiree homeowners) × (% with extractable equity) × (% who need cash) × (average loan size) × (origination fee rate of 1-2%)
steps: Step 1: Identify total US homeowners aged 60+ from census/demographic data
Step 2: Apply % who have sufficient home equity (e.g., equity > some threshold)
Step 3: Apply % who have a retirement income gap and would seek a loan
Step 4: Estimate average loan amount (e.g., fraction of home equity extracted)
Step 5: Multiply by origination fee rate (1-2%) to get revenue per loan
Step 6: Multiply by projected volume to get total addressable revenue
math.answer: Final market size depends on inputs; candidate is evaluated on process and logical structure, not a single numerical answer.

brainstorming.prompt: What are potential new product or revenue opportunities for a 401k/financial-services provider whose core customer base is aging retirees facing rising living costs?

categories.name: Liquidity / Home Equity Products
ideas: Retiree-specific home equity loan (no DTI requirement)
Home equity line of credit variant tailored for fixed-income seniors
Partnership with a bank or specialty lender to offer white-labeled mortgage products

categories.name: Healthcare / Longevity
ideas: Partnership with Medicare supplement or supplemental health insurers

categories.name: Income / Annuity Products
ideas: New annuity structures guaranteeing lifetime income
Variable annuity with enhanced withdrawal benefits

categories.name: Advisory / Planning Services
ideas: Fee-based retirement planning and drawdown strategy consulting
Digital / robo-advisor tier for lower-balance retirees

categories.name: New Customer Segments
ideas: Expand employer 403(b)/457 plan services to non-profit and government sectors
Serve pre-retirees aged 40-55 with accumulation-phase products
International expansion of retirement products to existing 8-country footprint

recommendation: The client should develop a new home-equity product specifically designed for retirees that does not require a debt-to-income ratio for approval, filling the gap between inaccessible mainstream products and predatory reverse mortgages

This product leverages the client's existing trusted relationships with its 55+ customer base, its scale (10 regional offices, 190+ Investor Centers), and its brand — giving it a meaningful competitive advantage over banks that do not specialize in the retiree segment
risks: Regulatory risk: entering mortgage lending requires new licenses and compliance infrastructure (CFPB, state lending laws, RESPA, TILA)
Credit/default risk: lending to income-poor retirees on home equity carries concentration risk if housing prices decline
Brand risk: any product perceived as predatory could damage the client's trusted brand with its core customer base
Execution risk: building or acquiring lending capabilities is a significant operational undertaking outside the client's current core competency
next_steps: Conduct detailed market sizing using demographic data on homeowners aged 60+ with extractable equity
Assess build vs. partner vs. acquire options for lending capability (partnering with an existing lender may be fastest to market)
Engage regulatory counsel to map licensing and compliance requirements
Run customer research with existing 55+ clients to validate product-market fit and willingness to use a home-equity product from this provider
Define pilot geography (e.g., one or two regional markets) to test before national rollout
